content: The prevention and control of Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) were addressed in a meeting coordinated by the WHO Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean. This meeting took place in Muscat, Oman, in December 2015. The discussions and recommendations from this meeting were subsequently published in a summary report in 2016. Participants in the meeting included representatives from the ministries of health and agriculture of the Islamic Republic of Iran, Oman, the Russian Federation, and Türkiye. Additionally, staff from the World Health Organization (WHO) and the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Atlanta, as well as infectious disease experts, laboratory scientists, and vector/tick control specialists, attended the meeting in their individual capacities as WHO Temporary Advisers. All WHO Temporary Advisers who participated in the meeting completed the required WHO declaration of interests. No conflicts of interest related to the subject matter of the meeting or with WHO were identified. The WHO Health Emergencies Infection Prevention and Control Readiness Team conducted a rapid literature search to provide contextual information, such as the epidemiology of CCHF. However, further evidence is required in specific areas, including the criteria for discontinuing isolation and discharging patients with confirmed CCHF, the risk of aerosol transmission of CCHF outside of aerosol-generating medical procedures, and the refinement of healthcare-associated infection (HAI) case definitions for CCHF in regions where national or localized definitions may not exist. As new evidence becomes available, the guidance will be revised and incorporated into future updates of the operational guide. The standing Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) Public Health Emergencies Working Group, composed of external experts, reviewed this document. Feedback was also obtained from various WHO units, including IPC focal points across the six WHO regions, and this input was integrated into the final document. Conflict of interest declaration forms for external reviewers were collected and reviewed in accordance with WHO policy. No conflicts of interest were identified. For further details on authorship and contributions, please refer to the acknowledgment section of the document. The WHO has also provided a range of resources related to CCHF, including guidelines, manuals, and reports. These resources cover topics such as the geographic distribution of CCHF, safe blood sample collection from suspected CCHF patients, and infection prevention and control measures in healthcare settings. Additionally, general IPC resources are available, including guidelines on core components of IPC programs, outbreak investigations, and improving indoor ventilation in the context of COVID-19. These resources are accessible through the WHO website and other platforms. The operational guide for infection prevention and control, as well as water, sanitation, and hygiene measures for CCHF in healthcare settings, is available in both electronic and print versions. It is published under the copyright of the World Health Organization, with some rights reserved under the Creative Commons IGO license.
